scams.name: String/Bracelet Friendship Scam
scams.description: Near Basilique Saint-Sernin, a vendor approaches tourists and ties a string or friendship bracelet around your wrist, claiming it is a 'cadeau' (gift). Once attached, they aggressively demand payment, often blocking your path until you pay. The bracelet is nearly impossible to remove quickly.
scams.avoidance: Keep hands in pockets when approached. Say 'Non merci' firmly and keep walking without stopping. Never let anyone tie anything on your wrist.

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: By the Canal du Midi or in tourist areas, a passer-by 'finds' a ring on the ground near you and claims it is 18-karat gold. They offer to sell it for 'gas money.' While you are distracted, an accomplice rifles through your bags or pockets. The ring is worthless brass.
scams.avoidance: Ignore any found jewelry and walk away immediately. Head toward the nearest busy cafe or shop if someone persists. Never engage in conversation about found items.
scams.location: Canal du Midi, tourist pedestrian areas, river quays

scams.name: Fake Petition/Deaf-Mute Charity Scam
scams.description: Young people, often pretending to be deaf-mute, approach tourists with clipboards asking for signatures on petitions for fake charities. After signing, they reveal a mandatory donation of 10-20 euros. Meanwhile, accomplices may pickpocket distracted victims.
scams.avoidance: Firmly say 'No' and walk away without stopping. Never sign anything on the street. These are organized groups and the money never goes to charity.
scams.location: Place du Capitole, Basilique Saint-Sernin, tourist attractions

scams.name: Metro and Public Transport Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets operate throughout Toulouse's metro system and buses, particularly during crowded rush hours. They work in groups where one person creates a distraction or crowding while accomplices steal wallets, phones, and valuables.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables in front pockets or secure cross-body bags. Be especially vigilant during boarding and exiting when crowds press together. Use money belts for large amounts of cash.
scams.location: Metro lines throughout city, bus stops, metro stations

scams.name: Gare Matabiau Train Station Theft
scams.description: Thefts and muggings are more common around Toulouse's central train station, Gare Matabiau, than in other parts of the city. The area between Rue Bayard and Allees Jean Jaures is particularly risky. Luggage theft and distraction pickpocketing are primary concerns.
scams.avoidance: Stay alert at the station and surrounding streets. Keep luggage close and use locks on bags. Avoid walking alone late at night. Use official taxi stands or pre-booked transport.
scams.location: Gare Matabiau, Rue Bayard, Allees Jean Jaures

scams.name: Fake Police ID Scam
scams.description: A stranger approaches asking you to break a large bill. Soon after, a 'police officer' appears with a story about illegal money exchange and asks to see your wallet for 'inspection.' They return it with half your cash missing. Scammers may wear armbands and carry fake badges.
scams.avoidance: Real French police never ask to see your wallet - only your ID removed from the wallet. Never hand over your wallet or phone. Ask to see police credentials and offer to walk to the nearest police station. If suspicious, dial 17.
scams.location: Metro stations, tourist areas, near ATMs

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging and Scams
scams.description: Some taxi drivers attempt to overcharge tourists by using nighttime tariffs during the day, taking unnecessarily long routes, or claiming the meter is broken. Unofficial taxis without proper markings may charge exorbitant rates.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxis with clearly marked 'TAXI' signs, visible taximeters, and displayed driver details. Ask for an estimate before starting and confirm the route. Note driver numbers if overcharged.
scams.location: Toulouse-Blagnac Airport, Gare Matabiau, city center

scams.name: Restaurant Tourist Trap Menu Scam
scams.description: Some restaurants offer cheap set menus displayed outside but present different, more expensive menus once seated. Other tactics include menus without prices, pushing medium or large portions only, and serving bottled water without asking. Some bars present inflated bills and use intimidation.
scams.avoidance: Check prices before ordering and confirm them verbally. Avoid restaurants with menus in many languages. Request the same menu shown outside. Always ask for 'une carafe d'eau' (tap water) which is free. Review your bill carefully.
scams.location: Place du Capitole, tourist-heavy streets, near major attractions

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Card Fraud
scams.description: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs that capture card data and PINs. Automated service stations and ATMs in tourist areas are frequently targeted. Some scammers approach ATM users offering to 'help' while watching PIN entry or claiming the machine is broken to steal inserted cards.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours. Cover the keypad completely when entering your PIN. Check for loose or unusual attachments on card slots. Never accept help from strangers at ATMs.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs, tourist areas, automated service stations

scams.name: Rose Seller Distraction Theft
scams.description: A scammer approaches with roses, offering one as a 'free gift.' Once you accept or touch it, they refuse to take it back and aggressively demand payment. While distracted by the confrontation, an accomplice quietly pickpockets your wallet, phone, or bag.
scams.avoidance: Never accept items from street vendors. Keep hands in pockets and say 'Non merci' firmly without breaking stride. Be aware of anyone positioning behind you during such encounters.
scams.location: Restaurant terraces, Place du Capitole, tourist areas

scams.name: Canal-Side Bicycle Grab Theft
scams.description: Thieves on bicycles target outdoor diners along the Canal du Midi and river quays. They rapidly grab phones, cameras, and bags from tables as they cycle past, making pursuit nearly impossible. The theft happens in seconds, often before victims can react.
scams.avoidance: Sit with your back against walls, facing outward. Never leave phones on tablecloths or table edges. Use wrist straps when filming or photographing. Keep bags on your lap or looped around chair legs.
scams.location: Canal du Midi, river quays, outdoor restaurant terraces

scams.name: Shell Game / Three-Card Monte
scams.description: A street operator sets up a game with three cups and a ball, shuffling quickly and inviting passersby to bet on finding the ball. The entire crowd including 'winners' are planted accomplices. The game uses sleight of hand making it impossible to win. While attention is focused on the game, accomplices pickpocket the crowd.
scams.avoidance: Never stop for street gambling games - they are illegal and always rigged. Walk away immediately if you see a crowd gathered around such games. Keep valuables secured.
